name: Quantum Mechanics II: Hilbrim
subtitle: Quantum Mechanics Course, Labs
shortDescription: Adaptive second course in quantum mechanics: spin, perturbation theory, scattering and Bell tests with five hands-on labs. Free to use.
longDescription:
Quantum Mechanics II: Hilbrim is a second undergraduate course in quantum mechanics, built to be practised, not just read. It follows the usual second-course syllabus: Dirac notation and Hilbert space, operators and commutators, spin-1/2 and the Bloch sphere, angular momentum and its addition, the hydrogen atom, time-independent perturbation theory, fine structure, Zeeman and Stark effects, the variational method, WKB, time-dependent perturbation theory and Rabi flopping, identical particles, scattering with Born and partial waves, density matrices, Bell inequalities and a first look at the Dirac equation.

### How It Adapts
Choose a personalised path or the syllabus order, and switch any time. The personalised path brings back questions on a spaced schedule, notices habits behind your wrong answers (for example a sign slip in second-order energy or forgetting to conjugate a bra) and aims practice at them, then moves you to the topics you are ready for. A course map shows all 16 topics and how they depend on each other, coloured by your mastery.

### Practice
140 original questions with typed numeric answers (fractions, square roots and pi are accepted) and multiple choice. Every numeric answer was checked by a second calculation engine. A full worked solution sits beside every answer and is always free. Unit checkpoints and timed mock exams use only code-verified questions.

### Five Labs
Spin-1/2 Bloch sphere and a Stern-Gerlach filter chain. A Clebsch-Gordan coupler. A perturbation shift plotter comparing exact levels with first and second order, up to strong-field Zeeman. A partial-wave scattering lab with phase shifts and the optical theorem. An entanglement and CHSH test with a sampled experiment.

### Learn At Any Level
Tap a concept for a plain explanation from earlier physics and maths, what it means in this course, and where it leads. Cited university courses, textbooks and papers open in a clear source window with the licence and a link.

### Free, With Ads At Natural Breaks
The course is free. Ads appear only at natural breaks, never during a test or before an explanation, and you can choose to watch a short video to earn extra mock exams. An optional monthly ad-free plan removes ads and unlocks unlimited mock exams. Price shown in the app before you subscribe; renews monthly, cancel any time in your account settings, with a 7-day free trial for new subscribers.

Not affiliated with any university, publisher or author named in the references.
